answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a public, time-delayed bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. The protocol caps how much work one bond can authorize and slashes it when independent audits prove fraud, so splitting funds across fake accounts does not multiply influence. A Sybil attacker must tie up real capital for the bond period and risks losing it; nectar, vertex, and falcon can be harmless account names, but none grants a free identity.
